title: Spicy Gochujang Galbi
shortDescription: A contemporary spicy galbi with flanken-cut beef ribs coated in gochujang, Korean pear, gochugaru, garlic, and sesame.
culturalContext: Soy-forward sweet-savory marinades are a familiar baseline for beef galbi. This gochujang-heavy version is explicitly a contemporary spicy adaptation developed for the locked inventory title, not a claim about a single traditional standard.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}

totalTime.display: 2 hours 45 minutes, including minimum marination and rest

equipment: Nonreactive mixing bowl or food-safe zip bag
Outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric tabletop grill

ingredients.item: flanken-cut beef short ribs, about 6 mm / 1/4 inch thick
ingredients.preparation: ask the butcher to remove bone dust; inspect each strip

allergenNotes: wheat/gluten may be present; check label
wheat/gluten may be present; check label

marinadeOrSeasoning.meatWeightCovered: 1.2 kg / 2.6 lb flanken-cut beef short ribs
mixOrder: Whisk gochujang, soy sauce, rice syrup, gochugaru, and rice vinegar until smooth.
Stir in pear, garlic, ginger, and sesame oil.
marinadeOrSeasoning.marinationVessel: Large nonreactive dish or food-safe zip bags on a rimmed tray
marinadeOrSeasoning.maximumPracticalMarinationWarning: Do not exceed 12 hours for thin ribs; pear, vinegar, salt, and chile paste can soften and over-season the surface.
marinadeOrSeasoning.reserveBeforeRawContactInstruction: Reserve any finishing glaze before raw ribs enter the marinade.
marinadeOrSeasoning.rawContactDiscardOrReboilInstruction: Discard all marinade that contacted raw beef; use only the clean reserved portion for finishing.
substitutions: Adjust heat with less gochugaru, not by removing gochujang without reformulating the salt and sugar balance.
Use certified gluten-free tamari and a verified gluten-free gochujang only after label review.
allergenNotes: Gochujang and soy sauce may contain wheat; verify both labels.

instructions.heading: Inspect and chill the ribs
instructions.action: Keep ribs cold, inspect the saw-cut surfaces, and remove visible loose bone fragments with a clean damp disposable towel. Do not rinse.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Rib strips are evenly thin and free of visible loose bone chips.
instructions.safetyNote: Sanitize surfaces after handling raw ribs; rinsing can spread contamination.

instructions.heading: Mix the spicy marinade
instructions.action: Whisk gochujang, soy sauce, rice syrup, gochugaru, and vinegar until smooth; stir in pear, garlic, ginger, and sesame oil.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The sauce is smooth, brick-red, and spoonable without dry chile clumps.
instructions.safetyNote: Reserve finishing glaze now, before adding raw beef.

instructions.heading: Marinate briefly
instructions.action: Coat ribs on both sides, cover, and refrigerate for 2 to 8 hours, turning once.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Each strip has a thin, even red coating rather than a heavy paste layer.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not marinate at room temperature or longer than 12 hours; discard raw-contact marinade.

instructions.heading: Preheat and reduce sticking
instructions.action: Preheat the approved grill to medium-high, clean it thoroughly, oil lightly, and let heavy excess marinade drip from the ribs.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Ribs sizzle promptly without the coating immediately burning.
instructions.safetyNote: Sugary gochujang can scorch; control heat rather than serving blackened coating as a doneness cue.

instructions.heading: Grill and turn
instructions.action: Grill in a single layer about 2 to 3 minutes per side, turning more often if hot spots darken the glaze.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The glaze is set and caramelized, not charred, and the thickest meat reaches target temperature.
instructions.safetyNote: Measure between bones without touching bone; transfer with clean utensils to a clean platter.

instructions.heading: Rest and finish safely
instructions.action: Rest at least 3 minutes. If desired, brush lightly with a clean reserved glaze warmed separately; never use raw-contact marinade.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The glaze remains glossy and red-brown, with the meat moist beneath it.
instructions.safetyNote: Identify bones clearly for diners, especially children.

grillSetup: Preheat a clean outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric tabletop grill to medium-high, about 400–450°F / 204–232°C. Follow the appliance manual for clearance and ventilation; never use charcoal, propane, butane camping stoves, or outdoor grills indoors.
targetInternalTemperature: 145°F / 63°C in the thickest practical portion, followed by a 3-minute rest
visualDonenessCues: Gochujang coating is set and caramelized but not blackened.
Thickest meat between bones reaches 145°F / 63°C and rests 3 minutes.
foodSafetyNotes: Keep raw beef and its marinade separate from ready-to-eat foods; wash hands and sanitize contacted surfaces.
Use separate raw and cooked plates and utensils, or wash and sanitize them fully before reuse.
Measure the thickest practical portion with a calibrated food thermometer; grill marks and time alone do not establish doneness.
For whole-cut beef, reach 145°F / 63°C and rest for at least 3 minutes before serving.
Use only an outdoor grill or an electric tabletop appliance explicitly approved by its manufacturer for indoor use; follow ventilation and clearance instructions.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Check every packaged-ingredient label and prevent cross-contact; substitutions do not guarantee an allergen-free result.

substitutions: For less heat, reduce gochugaru while retaining gochujang for body; verify the gochujang heat level on its label.
Gluten-related substitutions require both certified tamari and a verified gluten-free gochujang.
ingredientSourcing: Choose gochujang by declared heat level and inspect its soy and wheat allergen statement.
Request flanken ribs about 6 mm / 1/4 inch thick and ask the butcher to remove bone dust.
makeAhead: Mix the marinade up to 1 day ahead and refrigerate before raw contact. Marinate ribs 2 to 8 hours and never beyond 12 hours.
storage: Refrigerate cooked beef within 2 hours in a shallow airtight container at 40°F / 4°C or below; use within 3 days.
reheating: Reheat leftovers to 165°F / 74°C. Reheat only the portion needed and avoid prolonged cooking that toughens thin beef.
leftovers: Remove meat from bones, refrigerate promptly, and reheat to 165°F / 74°C. Use in rice bowls with fresh vegetables added after reheating.
servingSuggestions: Serve with rice and cooling fresh greens or cucumber dishes.
Offer additional clean sauce separately rather than pouring over the platter.

faq.question: Is spicy gochujang galbi a classic galbi formula?
faq.answer: This is explicitly a contemporary spicy variation. Classic beef galbi is commonly soy-forward, while gochujang and gochugaru define this adaptation.

faq.question: How do I keep the glaze from burning?
faq.answer: Drain excess marinade, use medium-high rather than maximum heat, turn around hot spots, and judge safety with a thermometer rather than dark color.
